prompt: Design a production-grade operating model for a multi-cell OpenStack private cloud. Cover user/API contracts, Keystone and service discovery, Nova API/cells/RPC/scheduler/compute, Placement, Glance, Neutron, Cinder, databases and messaging, desired versus effective state, identity and ownership, quotas/capacity/failure domains, security/multi-tenancy, observability, instance-build diagnosis, migrations/evacuation, backup/recovery, high availability, rolling upgrades, reconciliation, cleanup, governance, cost and explicit refusal conditions.
directAnswer: Model OpenStack as a set of independently owned asynchronous state machines joined by immutable request, project and resource identities. Authenticate and scope through Keystone, resolve a region/interface endpoint, pin API microversions and let each service authorize. Trace server creation through Nova API/global database, cell mapping, request spec, Placement candidates/allocation, scheduler claim, cell RPC/conductor/compute, then Glance bytes, Neutron port and effective dataplane, Cinder attachment/backend, hypervisor, guest and user flow. Version every service/config/database/message/API compatibility contract. Reconcile desired records with backend state rather than treating ACTIVE, bound or available as outcomes. Place databases, queues and service roles across real failure domains with tested quorum/fencing and capacity reserve. Protect management/service identities, endpoints, images, networks, volumes and audit. Correlate global request IDs and resource UUIDs. Upgrade by release procedure with prechecks, schema/online migrations, compatibility pins, canary cells, stop gates and recovery. Refuse ambiguous identity, stale catalog, unsupported microversion, unhealthy cell/RPC, stale Placement, missing image bytes, ineffective network, inconsistent volume/writer, unfenced host, insufficient reserve, incomplete migration, absent user evidence or unsafe cleanup.
foundation: The control plane accepts and coordinates intent; data-plane agents, backends and hypervisors realize it. Each database record, queue delivery and status belongs to a service boundary. Reliability requires correlating these boundaries without bypassing service ownership.
reasoningSteps: Define tenant user operations, state, SLO, isolation, RPO/RTO and lifecycle.
Inventory releases, service/API microversions, schemas, RPC/object compatibility and deployment tooling.
Design Keystone domains/projects/roles/service users/tokens/catalog and downstream policies.
Separate public/internal/admin endpoints and protect transport, credentials and audit.
Map Nova global API state, cell mappings, cell0, per-cell databases/queues/conductors and compute hosts.
Define request IDs, server UUIDs and evidence correlation across services.
Model request spec, Placement providers/inventory/traits/candidates/allocations and scheduler claim.
Admit computes by capability, maintenance, aggregate/AZ and failure-domain policy.
Control Glance provenance, import/staging, stores, access, integrity and lifecycle.
Map Neutron network/subnet/port/router/security state to bindings, agents/controllers and packet paths.
Map Cinder volume/snapshot/attachment records to scheduler, service, backend and connector state.
Define one-writer authority, fencing and supported reconciliation for partial operations.
Set per-project quotas plus physical capacity and recovery reserve.
Design database and messaging clustering from consistency and failure semantics.
Scale API, scheduler, conductor, agents and workers with service-specific HA requirements.
Correlate logs, notifications, metrics and traces by request/resource/project/cell/host.
Diagnose BUILD/ERROR/ACTIVE from the first divergent boundary, not last visible status.
Preflight migration and evacuation for host authority, Placement, network, storage and service readiness.
Back up service databases/config/keys and prove ordered isolated recovery.
Upgrade by supported release sequence, schema expansion, service compatibility and online migrations.
Canary one failure domain, set user/data stop gates and preserve rollback/recovery limits.
Reconcile orphan allocations, ports, attachments, images and instances through supported service APIs/tools.
Prove cleanup and audit for every partial request.
Govern ownership, deprecation, capacity, image/volume lifecycle, cost and incident review.
Keep conclusions bounded to the exact release, topology, workload and test window.
seniorAnswer: I operate OpenStack as a distributed workflow, not a dashboard. Keystone scope/catalog and service policy establish request authority. Nova global and cell-local state, Placement claims, Glance bytes, Neutron effective dataplane, Cinder backend attachment and compute execution each need correlated evidence before the user flow is ready. Cells and HA isolate failure only when databases, queues, service roles, capacity and fencing are designed accordingly. Upgrades are release-specific compatibility campaigns with canary, migrations, stop and recovery. I refuse ambiguous identity, unsupported contracts, record/backend drift, unfenced writers, insufficient reserve or missing user proof.
weakAnswer: Deploy three controllers behind HAProxy, use Galera and RabbitMQ clusters, enable all OpenStack services and monitor their process status.
whyWeak: Product count and process availability omit token/catalog/policy, cell boundaries, Placement claims, effective network/storage/image state, quorum/fencing semantics, capacity reserve, release compatibility, request correlation, recovery, cleanup and user outcomes.

evidence.signal: Versioned topology and service compatibility matrix
evidence.proves: Named components and supported interactions in the reviewed design

evidence.signal: Correlated request journal across service records and backends
evidence.proves: Observed state transitions and first divergence for covered operations

evidence.signal: Canary upgrade, online migration and rollback journal

followUps.answer: They shard and isolate cell-local database and messaging work, but global API state and cross-cell operations still require explicit design.
It tracks provider inventory, traits and allocations and returns candidates; Nova still builds the request, selects and claims a destination and computes still realize it.

followUps.prompt: What does a bound Neutron port prove?
followUps.answer: A control-plane binding decision exists; effective host/controller flows and end-to-end packet behavior remain separate evidence.

followUps.prompt: What makes a rolling upgrade safe?
followUps.answer: Supported version adjacency, API/RPC/object/database compatibility, ordered migrations, canary and stop gates, preserved recovery and user/data validation.

rubric.observableEvidence: Defines operations, identities, microversions, scope, endpoints and policy
Maps global/cell databases, cell0, RPC, conductor, scheduler and compute
Controls inventory, traits, allocations, claim, quota, reserve and failure domains
Controls provenance, stores, import, access, integrity and retirement
Maps desired records to effective dataplane/backend and writer authority
Uses least privilege, protected endpoints, isolation, keys/secrets and audit
Correlates request/resource evidence and finds first divergent boundary
Designs dependency HA, quorum/fencing, reserve, restore and validation
Uses compatibility, migrations, canary, stop, rollback and orphan cleanup
Defines ownership, lifecycle, cost, refusal conditions and bounded claims
